title: wt refs restore <runId> --yes --json
description: What `wt refs restore <runId> --yes` put back. Printed by `wt refs restore <runId> --yes --json` as the only thing on stdout, also when a handled SIGINT or SIGTERM ends the run. Schema 1: fields may be added and enumerations may gain values; nothing is renamed or removed. See docs/json.md.

runId.description: The run id as given; one not in wt's format is an error.

token.description: The token of the plan the run went by.

outcome.description: done: every selected row was restored. refused: nothing changed. partial: some were, some not. interrupted: a signal ended the run.

id.description: refs/heads/<name> or refs/tags/<name> here; origin:refs/heads/<name> or origin:refs/tags/<name> on origin. --only takes it, one id per flag and never split: a ref name may contain a comma.

action.description: create: the name is free; it is made at object. none: it is already there at object; only the pin goes. occupied: the name holds another object here. remoteOccupied: origin has something there. endpointChanged: a remote ref, and origin no longer resolves to the URLs the run recorded in its meta. endpointUnknown: a remote ref, and the run has no meta. pinGone: the pin is not there any more; a pin that goes between the plan and the run is reported as kept, its reason starting pinGone.

result.description: restored: the ref is at object and the pin is gone. kept: left alone on purpose (reason says). failed: tried and not finished. notRun: the run ended before it. interrupted: a signal caught it. notSelected: not selected.

restored.description: The ref holds object, read back after the row.

pinDeleted.description: The pin is gone, read back after the row.
